title: Stability and Sabbatical Policy — All‑Hands
summary: Company all‑hands focused on service reliability metrics, recent incidents, and a proposed sabbatical / extended leave policy. Leadership shared operational levers, hiring posture, and changes to on‑call rotations. Open Q&A covered pay parity, eligibility, and how sabbatical interacts with reserved capacity contracts.
topics: SRE review: incidents and stability trends
People update: sabbatical proposal and eligibility
Changes to on‑call and burnout mitigations
action_items: Ava Patel - Publish full sabbatical policy draft to handbook and share feedback doc (due 2027-09-08)
Diego Ramos - Deliver postmortem summary of July 27 P99 outage to engineering and product (due 2027-08-30)
Priya Menon - Start 2‑week pilot of reduced page noise thresholds and report metrics (due 2027-09-10)
Riley Park - Update hiring timeline and prioritize two SRE roles for Q4 (due 2027-09-03)
next_steps: Run a benefits town hall to walk through sabbatical scenarios (Ava)
Share a short pulse survey about on‑call load and burnout (People Ops)
Ops to propose a concrete on‑call rotation change and fallback coverage plan
questions: How will sabbatical affect eligibility for reserved capacity discounts?
Can sabbatical time be taken for caregiving vs personal development?
Will headcount targets change given the new SRE hiring priority?
meeting_header: Date: 2027-08-25 | Start: 10:00 PDT | Duration: ~62m | Location: All‑Hands (Zoom)
transcript:
00:00 Michael Chen: okay everyone, uh let's get started a little after 10. thanks for coming in, we have a packed agenda today — stability, people policy, and a few ops items. gonna hand off to Diego for the SRE review first
00:22 Diego Ramos: thanks mike. quick note, we have the slide deck in the drive, link in the chat — but highlights first; the July 27 outage was the biggest disruption, P99 went to 2.8s for about 18 minutes, root cause was a cascade from a batch job change that increased gpu warmup pressure, and KV cache churn wasn't handled well.
00:45 Diego Ramos: we rolled to fallback model variants and autoscale more aggressively which helped, but, um, we need better preflight for batch jobs — we had some mistaken thresholds. open to questions but I'll go through the metrics.
01:05 Priya Menon (SRE): yeah hi — and there was some telemetry blind spots, prefix cache eviction wasn't emitting the right metric under high mem pressure. we've patched it, but we want to run a week of synthetic load to validate.
01:20 Michael Chen: can you quantify customer impact, Diego? any large accounts hit?
01:30 Diego Ramos: two larger hosted customers saw degraded throughput, latency spikes; no data exfil, but user‑facing timeouts happened. finance flagged a potential crediting exposure, tom's on it.
01:45 Tom Wallace: confirmed, we have a draft impact assessment; visible MRR hit is small but the risk is reputational, so we recommended review with sales ops.
02:05 Michael Chen: okay thanks. Samira, any product viewpoint?
02:12 Samira Khan: from product side we saw retry storms in client SDKs, some customers increased concurrency to compensate which made it worse. we plan to publish recommended client settings and push updates in SDK 1.7.
02:30 Jordan Lee: question — did we revert the batch job change or patch it?
02:35 Diego Ramos: we reverted the job. long term fix is a gating check in CI and a safe deploy flag.
02:50 Michael Chen: good. next section, Ava will share people update — sabbatical policy proposal and why we're doing it now.
03:05 Ava Patel: hey folks, thanks. quick context: we've had repeated asks for a formal sabbatical offering, and with the hiring runway improving we think it's time to pilot a formal program to reduce burnout and reward longer tenures. high level: eligibility at 4 years full‑time, 8 weeks paid sabbatical, up to 12 weeks unpaid optional, re‑entry benefits, and a manager approval flow.
03:32 Ava Patel: we know the tricky bits — comp, equity vesting treatment, reserved capacity customers who are on long contracts — so we're drafting policy language and want feedback from managers and ICs.
03:45 Riley Park: will sabbatical be pro‑rated for people who were part time or intern then full time?
03:50 Ava Patel: great question. proposal is to count total continuous employment at Redwood, with a small exceptions window for parental leaves; intern time won't accrue sabbatical credit. we'll note specific edge cases in the draft.
04:10 Tom Wallace: curious about payroll and budgeting — eight weeks paid is material. can we afford it at scale?
04:18 Michael Chen: we modelled scenarios — samira and i ran some headcount burn models. at current hiring rates it looks manageable if we prioritize SRE and shift some contractor spend. we'll share the spreadsheet after.
04:35 Samira Khan: also note sabbatical could help retention, which is cheaper than hiring.
04:40 Michael Chen: yep. next up, on‑call changes: Diego?
04:45 Diego Ramos: right. current rotation has two SREs primary / two backup, frequency every 4 weeks. feedback from the pulse survey shows people are fatigued, especially juniors. proposal: move to 6 week rotations for primary with a dedicated weekend responder pool, limit overnight followups, and raise the threshold for low‑priority pages during PST late night windows.
05:10 Priya Menon: we've seen a lot of alert noise from ephemeral infra things; small changes to thresholds remove ~30% of pages in our staging runs.
05:25 Michael Chen: are customer SLAs impacted by lowering page sensitivity?
05:30 Diego Ramos: we'll route critical errors (errors causing dropped requests or data loss) to pages unchanged; only noisy, low‑severity perf regressions get smoothed. the automated fallback policies (model variants) preserve customer experience for most gen use cases.
05:50 Jordan Lee: any change to escalation?
05:54 Diego Ramos: escalation stays, but we add a daily overlap shift for cross‑region coverage to avoid late‑night wakes.
06:05 Michael Chen: alright. we're at about 6 minutes in but we're moving through topics, folks — apologies I misstated the timer earlier, we'll keep the Q&A open at the end. next topic: hiring posture and prioritization.
06:22 Samira Khan: hiring — we will fast‑track two SRE hires and one infra‑focused ML engineer for Q4. recruiting will prioritize candidates with production serving experience. Riley will share timelines.
06:34 Riley Park: yes, we have active pipeline, we'll push two offers by early September if interviews go well. we also propose retrofitting a contractor to staff conversion if needed.
06:44 Michael Chen: finance perspective?
06:47 Tom Wallace: small budget shift is fine, we're de‑prioritizing a marketing headcount to keep spend neutral for the quarter.
06:55 Ava Patel: one people note — sabbatical eligibility will not reduce promotion consideration; in other words taking sabbatical won't gate advancement. we want to avoid perverse incentives.
07:10 Attendee 1 (Lena Ortiz): quick ops question — how does sabbatical affect on‑call rotation if a senior is out for 8 weeks? do we hire temp coverage?
07:20 Ava Patel: we'll require a coverage plan as part of approval: reassign duties, hire short‑term contractor, or shift rotation temporarily. managers must submit coverage options.
07:32 Michael Chen: thanks. okay let's take a short break and then return for Q&A.
07:40 -- short pause --
08:10 Michael Chen: back. open mic Q&A. I'll moderate quickly so we can capture key items.
08:20 Attendee 2 (Jordan Lee): on the infra incident, is there a plan to change CI gating to catch the batch job regressions earlier?
08:28 Diego Ramos: yes, adding a performance smoke test in CI that simulates warmup pressure, plus a canary rollout window for heavy batch jobs.
08:35 Attendee 3 (Priya Menon): will the ticketing taxonomy change? we spent a lot of time triaging noisy alerts into meaningful incidents.
08:40 Diego Ramos: good point — yes, we'll refine alerts to incident categories and add automated dedupe heuristics.
08:46 Attendee 4 (Tom Wallace): payroll question — if someone takes paid sabbatical and their equity cliff is mid‑sabbatical, does cliff pause?
08:55 Ava Patel: cliff treatments are one of the open items; current proposal is vesting continues as normal for paid sabbatical, unpaid will pause vesting but count toward tenure for eligibility — we want to keep it simple but fair. will finalize in the draft.
09:10 Attendee 5 (Riley Park): hiring metric — if we prioritize SRE, does that push back product hires?
09:16 Samira Khan: a little, but we think the tradeoff is worth it for stability. product hiring will continue for critical roadmap items.
09:25 Michael Chen: we're nearing the end — a couple lightning items: leadership is instituting monthly reliability review meetings that will be public to the company, and a short pulse survey will go out tomorrow to gather more granular on‑call load facts.
09:40 Jordan Lee: can we get the synthetic load test schedule?
09:45 Priya Menon: yes, we target week of Sept 6 for initial run, details in the runbook link in chat.
09:55 Michael Chen: okay, final wrap: recap of action items, Ava will publish draft sabbatical policy, Diego will deliver the postmortem, Priya will run the page noise pilot, Riley will accelerate SRE hiring. we want feedback on the policy by Sept 8.
10:15 Attendee 6 (Lena Ortiz): one last ask — can we add mental health days as separate from sabbatical? it's a demand we've heard frequently.
10:25 Ava Patel: yes, that is on the roadmap, mental health days will be discussed in the next people forum.
10:40 Michael Chen: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the doc links, the spreadsheet and the postmortem. meeting adjourned.
